en: vt. to change something to make it suitable for a new use or situation; to change a book or play so it can be used in a film or on TV; vi. to get used to a new situation
ex: It took him a few months to adapt to his new school.
他花了幾個月才適應新學校。

en: n. a strip of cloth used to cover and protect a wound or injury; vt. to cover a wound with a bandage
ex: The nurse wrapped a bandage around his injured arm.
護理師在他受傷的手臂上纏了一圈繃帶。

en: a. very unhappy or uncomfortable; very bad or unpleasant; (of a person) mean and unkind; (of a small amount) not enough
ex: She felt miserable after failing the exam.
她考試不及格後覺得很難過。
ph: 讓某人的生活痛苦不堪

en: n. a very strong feeling of dislike for someone or something
ex: He felt deep hatred for those who had hurt his family.
他對傷害他家人的人懷有深深的恨意。

en: n. a feeling of very great sadness, especially when someone dies; something that causes great sadness; trouble or disaster
ex: She was overcome with grief when her grandmother died.
外婆過世時，她悲痛欲絕。

en: n. a substance found in food such as meat, fish, eggs and beans that is necessary for the body to grow and stay healthy; a. rich in protein
ex: Eggs and fish are good sources of protein.
蛋和魚是很好的蛋白質來源。

en: a. clear and not likely to change; certain or sure; having clear limits or boundaries
ex: We need a definite answer by tomorrow.
我們明天前需要一個明確的答覆。

en: n. a unit of sound in a word that has one vowel sound; vt. to divide a word into syllables
ex: The word "banana" has three syllables.
「banana」這個字有三個音節。

en: n. something that you are trying to achieve; (grammar) the case used for the object of a verb; a. based on facts and not influenced by personal feelings; real and not imaginary
ex: The objective of the meeting is to agree on a new plan.
會議的目標是就新計畫達成共識。

en: a. willing to accept other people's behavior, beliefs or opinions without criticizing them; able to endure unpleasant conditions; (of a plant or animal) able to survive in certain conditions
ex: She is very tolerant of other people's mistakes.
她對別人的錯誤非常寬容。

en: a. belonging to an early stage of development; very simple and basic; (of a society) not having developed modern technology; n. a person from an early or ancient culture
ex: Primitive people used stones to make tools.
原始人用石頭製作工具。

en: n. the act of saying no to something; the act of refusing something; the right to be the first to buy something
ex: His refusal to cooperate made the situation worse.
他拒絕合作，使情況更糟。

en: n. a large sea animal with a hard shell, a long body and big claws, eaten as food; the meat of this animal
ex: We ate grilled lobster at the seaside restaurant.
我們在海邊餐廳吃了烤龍蝦。

en: n. an idea or principle that is formed in the mind; a general idea about something; a general notion or plan
ex: It is hard to grasp the concept of infinity.
很難理解無限這個概念。

en: a. continuing for a period of time without a break; happening without stopping; (in grammar) showing an action that is still going on
ex: There was a continuous noise coming from the construction site.
工地傳來持續不斷的噪音。

en: a. strange and not easily understood; difficult to explain or understand; secret or hidden
ex: A mysterious light appeared in the sky last night.
昨晚天空出現了一道神秘的光。

en: n. a person who steals money or property, often using force or threats
ex: The robber ran away with the bag full of cash.
搶匪帶著裝滿現金的袋子逃走了。

en: n. the quality of being easy to use or suitable for your needs; something that makes life easier or more comfortable; a time that is suitable for you
ex: I live near the station for the convenience.
我住在車站附近是為了方便。

en: a. easy to carry or move; able to be used on a computer in different places; n. a small building that can be moved
ex: I bought a portable charger for my phone.
我買了一個手機行動電源。

en: n. a careful examination of the facts about something, especially a crime; a detailed study of a subject
ex: The police have launched an investigation into the fire.
警方已展開對這場火災的調查。

en: n. the official home or office of an ambassador in a foreign country; the group of officials working in an embassy
ex: She went to the embassy to apply for a visa.
她去大使館申請簽證。

en: n. an instrument for looking at distant objects, especially stars and planets; vi. to become shorter by sliding one part into another; vt. to shorten something by pushing parts into each other
ex: He looked at the moon through a telescope.
他透過望遠鏡看月亮。

en: n. a very frightening dream; an experience or situation that is very unpleasant or frightening; a very bad person or thing
ex: I woke up from a terrible nightmare.
我從一場可怕的噩夢中醒來。

en: vt. to control someone or something by having more power or influence; to be the most important or noticeable part of something; vi. to have the most power or influence
ex: The company dominates the global smartphone market.
這家公司主導全球智慧型手機市場。

en: vt. to make someone laugh or smile; to keep someone interested and happy; to provide someone with entertainment
ex: The clown amused the children with funny tricks.
小丑用有趣的把戲逗樂了孩子們。

en: a. (informal) very bad or of very poor quality; (informal) feeling ill; covered with lice; (informal) unpleasant
ex: I had a lousy day at work yesterday.
我昨天工作過得很糟。

en: n. a way of entering a place; the right or ability to use or enter something; a way of getting information from a computer; vt. to get information from a computer; to reach or enter a place
ex: You need a password to access the account.
你需要密碼才能存取該帳戶。

en: a. showing or accepting things as they really are; seeming like real life; able to be achieved
ex: We need to set realistic goals for this project.
我們需要為這個專案設定切實的目標。

en: a. happening at the end of a process or period of time; occurring as a final result
ex: The eventual winner of the race was a young runner from Kenya.
這場比賽最終的贏家是一位來自肯亞的年輕跑者。

en: n. a strong feeling that you will do something, no matter how hard; the act of deciding something; the process of finding out something exactly
ex: She showed great determination in finishing the marathon.
她展現了完成馬拉松的堅定決心。

en: a. relating to the economy, trade and money; making a profit; not wasteful
ex: The government has announced a new economic policy.
政府已公布一項新的經濟政策。

en: a. existing in large amounts; more than enough; (of food or resources) available in large quantities
ex: Fresh fruit is plentiful in summer.
夏天新鮮水果很豐富。

en: vi. to begin to exist or become noticeable; to happen as a result of something; to get up from a sitting or lying position; to rise
ex: A problem arose when the machine stopped working.
機器停止運作時出現了一個問題。

en: a. (of soil) able to grow strong healthy crops; able to have babies or young; full of new ideas
ex: The valley has fertile soil and is good for farming.
這個山谷土壤肥沃，適合耕作。

en: vt. to go somewhere with someone; to happen at the same time as something else; to play a musical instrument while someone sings; vi. to play music while someone sings
ex: She will accompany her mother to the hospital tomorrow.
她明天會陪媽媽去醫院。

en: a. done in a relaxed way without hurry; (of a person) not in a hurry; adv. in a relaxed and unhurried way
ex: We took a leisurely walk along the river.
我們沿著河邊悠閒地散步。

en: vt. to send someone away or tell them they can go; to remove someone from a job; to decide that something is not worth considering; vi. to leave or to be allowed to leave
ex: The boss dismissed him for being late again.
老闆因他又遲到而解僱了他。

en: n. the act of taking part in something; the act of sharing in something with others
ex: Student participation is very important in this class.
學生的參與在這堂課非常重要。

en: n. the scientific study of the structure of substances and how they react; the chemical structure of something; a feeling of attraction between two people
ex: She studies chemistry at university and wants to be a scientist.
她在大學念化學，想當科學家。

en: vt. to succeed in doing or completing something; to finish something successfully; n. something that is achieved
ex: She accomplished her goal of running a marathon.
她達成了跑完馬拉松的目標。
